profile.campus: Secaucus / North Bergen, Hudson County, New Jersey (Equinix New York metro campus)
profile.reading:
Equinix's own facility page places this building, NY6, at 105 Enterprise Avenue South in Secaucus, New Jersey 07094, describing a one story, steel frame structure of 16,393 square feet, the smallest of the five Secaucus buildings tracked in this registry. Published specifications list N+1 generator redundancy with 30 or more hours of autonomy at full load, N+2 cooling redundancy, and a minimum cabinet density of 5kVA. UPS redundancy is not disclosed on the page. The building is listed above the 500 year base flood elevation, with a double interlock pre action fire suppression system and 24/7 security using biometric access and mantraps. Equinix advertises a 99.9999 percent plus global uptime guarantee and describes the customer base in general terms as large financial, media, and enterprise companies. No megawatt capacity figure and no year of construction are published on Equinix's own NY6 page.

NY6 is one of five Equinix buildings, NY2 through NY6, addressed within roughly a mile of each other around Secaucus in Hudson County, all appearing together on Equinix's own New York metro location listing. Data Center Frontier, a trade publication, reported in 2026 that Equinix's broader New York and New Jersey metro area totals nine IBX buildings and about 739,000 square feet of technical space, and it profiled one of those buildings, NY5, in some detail. NY5 was built in 2012 and expanded in 2016 to 20 megawatts of critical power capacity, fed by four utility lines and backed by eight 2.5 megawatt generators, with the campus staying online for a full week without grid power during Superstorm Sandy in 2012. That 20 megawatt figure describes NY5 specifically, a separate and larger building from NY6, and Equinix's own NY6 page does not publish a comparable power number for this small building. Given its size, NY6 most likely functions as a smaller edge or overflow location within the Secaucus cluster rather than a primary hosting hall, though Equinix does not state this directly and this registry treats it as a reasonable inference rather than a published fact.

Equinix was founded in 1998 by Al Avery and Jay Adelson and has grown into a global colocation and interconnection company running more than 260 IBX data centers across more than 70 metro areas, converting to a real estate investment trust in 2015. Hudson County's Equinix cluster sits roughly ten miles from Lower Manhattan, shaped by lower New Jersey real estate costs and proximity to the Wall Street financial corridor rather than any single anchor tenant.
profile.campus_sqft: Published individual square footage for four of the five Secaucus buildings totals 550,057 sq ft (NY2 131,040 + NY3 250,853 + NY4 151,771 + NY6 16,393 per Equinix's own site). NY5's individual square footage is not published by Equinix. The wider 9-site Equinix New York/New Jersey metro area totals roughly 739,000 sq ft of technical space per Data Center Frontier (2026).

profile.regional_context: Equinix describes NY3 (Secaucus) as its largest New York metro site, serving major financial, media, and enterprise companies with an Ad-IX advertising exchange and cloud on-ramps.
profile.campus_power_note: Equinix has not published a building specific megawatt figure for NY2, NY3, NY4, or NY6. The only building specific power figure publicly reported for the 5-building Secaucus campus is NY5's 20 MW of critical power capacity (built 2012, expanded 2016), per Data Center Frontier (2026). That figure belongs to NY5 only and should not be read onto any other building in this cluster.
profile.facility_type_note: Part of Equinix's New York metro campus. The New Jersey facilities in this registry (Hudson County, Middlesex County, North Bergen, Secaucus) correspond to Equinix's Secaucus campus (NY2-NY6), while NY1 (the historic 165 Halsey Street carrier hotel in Newark, also tied to a Tishman operator record elsewhere in this registry) and other NY-branded buildings (NY7, NY9, NY11, and upstate NY13 in Elmsford) complete the 10-facility metro per Equinix's own site.

reading.body:
Equinix NY6 is a 16,393-square-foot colocation facility in Secaucus, New Jersey, part of Equinix's larger nine-building New York metro campus. The facility publishes N+2 cooling redundancy and a minimum cabinet density of 5 kW per rack, but does not publish its total power capacity. Using the stated 5 kW minimum density and the published square footage, a floor fully populated at that density would support roughly 330 racks consuming approximately 1.7 MW, though this represents only a floor-by-floor estimate and not an operator claim about total campus capacity.

The Secaucus cluster, anchored by the neighboring NY5 building with 20 megawatts of critical power and four utility feeder lines, proved resilient during Superstorm Sandy in 2012 and has drawn major financial services tenants seeking proximity to Wall Street without Manhattan's space constraints. This campus sits in Hudson County, where Equinix has concentrated its largest East Coast metro footprint due to lower real estate costs and direct access to the financial corridor. The facility qualifies for Equinix Fabric software-defined interconnection and direct cloud on-ramps to AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle Cloud, and IBM Cloud, supporting private cages and cross-connects for enterprises and institutional traders.

New Jersey has 48 mapped data center facilities, of which only five publish power capacity figures totaling 111.3 MW. Equinix NY6's specific power capacity is not published by the operator, placing this facility among the vast majority of US data centers that do not disclose their critical power figures. Within the state's published capacity, the wider Secaucus campus ranks sixth.
